Test homogeneity of variance for multiple variables at once

Source: R/vtest.R
vtest.Rd

This function performs Levene's test for homogeneity of variance on multiple variables in a dataframe. For each variable, it tests whether the variance is the same in all groups. It returns the results in a tidy format.

Usage

vtest(df, cols, group, center = c("median", "mean"))

Arguments

df

A dataframe containing the data to be tested. It can be supplied directly (vtest(df = mtcars, ...)) or piped into the function (mtcars |> vtest(...)).

cols

<tidy-select> The numeric variables to test, written as unquoted column names, e.g. mpg or c(mpg, disp). Selection helpers such as starts_with() or where(is.numeric) also work. Grouping variables are never tested.

group

<tidy-select> The variable that defines the groups to compare, written as an unquoted column name, e.g. cyl. If you select several variables, e.g. c(cyl, am), every combination of their values is treated as a separate group, as needed for a factorial (e.g. two-way) ANOVA.

center

The value each group is centred on: "median" (the default) or "mean". "median" is the default in car::leveneTest() and is more robust when the data are not normally distributed (it is also known as the Brown-Forsythe test). "mean" gives the original Levene's test, which is what SPSS reports.

Value

A tibble with one row per variable and the columns variable, statistic (the F statistic), df1 and df2 (the degrees of freedom), p.value and method.

Details

Levene's test checks the assumption of homogeneity of variance (also called homoscedasticity), which tests such as the t-test and ANOVA rely on. For each variable, it measures how far each value is from the centre (median or mean) of its group and then compares these distances across groups with a one-way ANOVA. A significant result (e.g. p.value < 0.05) suggests that the variances differ between groups. The results are identical to those of car::leveneTest().

Before running any tests, the function checks that df is a dataframe, that all variables in cols are numeric, that there are at least two groups, that each group has at least two non-missing values, and that the values are not identical within every group. If any check fails, the function stops with an error message explaining which variables or groups are affected.

Missing values are handled separately for each variable, so a missing value in one variable does not remove that row from the tests of other variables. Rows with a missing value in group are removed, and a short message says how many.

Groups are defined only by group. If df is already a grouped dataframe, that grouping is ignored and a short message says so (unless it matches group).

See also

ntest() and ntest_by() to test the assumption of normality

Other assumption tests: ntest(), ntest_by()

Examples

# Compare the variance of mpg across the groups of cyl
vtest(df = mtcars, cols = mpg, group = cyl)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   variable statistic   df1   df2 p.value method                         
#>   <chr>        <dbl> <int> <int>   <dbl> <chr>                          
#> 1 mpg           5.51     2    29 0.00939 Levene's test (center = median)

# Test several variables, piping the data into the function
mtcars |> vtest(c(mpg, disp, hp), cyl)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   variable statistic   df1   df2 p.value method                         
#>   <chr>        <dbl> <int> <int>   <dbl> <chr>                          
#> 1 mpg           5.51     2    29 0.00939 Levene's test (center = median)
#> 2 disp          3.29     2    29 0.0516  Levene's test (center = median)
#> 3 hp            2.91     2    29 0.0705  Levene's test (center = median)

# Use the mean instead of the median (the original Levene's test)
vtest(mtcars, mpg, cyl, center = "mean")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   variable statistic   df1   df2 p.value method                       
#>   <chr>        <dbl> <int> <int>   <dbl> <chr>                        
#> 1 mpg           6.48     2    29 0.00470 Levene's test (center = mean)

# Compare all combinations of two grouping variables
vtest(mtcars, mpg, group = c(cyl, am))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   variable statistic   df1   df2 p.value method                         
#>   <chr>        <dbl> <int> <int>   <dbl> <chr>                          
#> 1 mpg           2.74     5    26  0.0409 Levene's test (center = median)
